stable_useful_signals: Both briefs preserve the decision question and action consequence.
Both briefs preserve source refs, source status, uncertainty, privacy limits, and evidence-only exclusions.
Both briefs preserve non-claims, including no product proof, no human validation, no answer-quality scoring, no runtime sidecar update, and no action authorization.
Both briefs remain readable while naming their generated-read supply origin.
unstable_or_weak_signals: The generated-read briefs are thinner than earlier enriched briefs.
Fields such as lost_value, noisy_friction, live_options, and assistant_influence_on_user_framing remain evidence-only or excluded.
A readable generated-read brief can create overtrust risk, especially in domain-sensitive workflow contexts.
repeated_source_depth_risks: Both briefs depend on checked-in-safe generated-read supply rather than full private conversation context.
Both briefs require human review before operational use.
Both briefs cannot prove semantic truth or advice correctness.
repeated_overclaim_risks: Readable Markdown can make provisional generated-read supply feel more complete than it is.
Launch-beta can be overread as product evidence.
Deploy-intake can be overread as operational, legal, compliance, or clinical clearance.
readability_pattern: Readable and inspectable across two decision families, provided the generated-read origin and non-claims remain visible.
evidence_and_limits_pattern: The renderer repeatedly keeps source refs, source status, uncertainty, privacy limits, evidence-only exclusions, and non-claims visible.
